summary: Adds a /download endpoint that serves files from the upload directory by name. It also changes the dev server to bind all interfaces with debug mode on.

findings.title: Path traversal in download endpoint
findings.problem: The download handler joins the name query parameter onto UPLOAD_DIR without any containment check. A name like ../../etc/passwd or an absolute path such as /etc/passwd escapes UPLOAD_DIR.
findings.consequence: Any client can read any file the server process can read. This exposes secrets, config files and source code.
findings.fix: Resolve the joined path and reject it unless it stays under UPLOAD_DIR. Alternatively use send_from_directory, which enforces that boundary.

findings.title: Debug server exposed on all interfaces
findings.problem: The change turns on debug mode and binds the server to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1. Debug mode enables the interactive Werkzeug debugger.
findings.consequence: Anyone on the network can reach the debugger and may run arbitrary code on the host. Error pages also leak source and environment details.
findings.fix: Keep the 127.0.0.1 binding and read the debug flag from the environment, defaulting to off.

findings.title: New download endpoint has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds the download handler with a 404 path and a file-serving path. The repository contains no test that exercises either path.
findings.consequence: Regressions in path handling, including traversal guards, would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for a valid file, a missing file and a traversal attempt.

dropped.reason: The finding raised for c1 already covers the 0.0.0.0 binding on this line.
